description.text:
A trade-off between warping things well for nearby frames vs. frames further away. For example, if you want to warp up to 20-30 frames away from the reference frame, it's better to go for a value closer to '1 frame'. For warps over 100 frames away, you can set this closer to '64 frames'. 

Each shot will have its own optimum 'frame distance' value so experiment a bit to find the best value. 

For high motion shots, you should set this value closer to '1 frame'. Shots with low motion can be set closer to '64 frames'.

This is the GPU that will be used for rendering, when Use GPU if available is selected. If you have more than one GPU in your machine, you can select a different GPU Device to use by editing your Preferences. (Note that selecting a different GPU will require a restart of Nuke to take effect.) Local GPU will be shown as Not available when any of the following is true: * Use CPU is selected as the GPU Device in your Preferences. * No suitable GPU was found on your system. Please refer to the documentation for details of the requirements for GPU acceleration. * It was not possible to create a context for processing on the selected GPU. For example, this can happen when there is not enough free memory available on the GPU. To use the GPU when rendering from the command line, add --gpu to your command.
This filter is used to apply the warp to the image, it has the same effect as that of the filters used in the IDistort and ST-map nodes.

Controls how the paint pushed from the keyframes are blended together, there are 3 options: warped src, warp the 'Src' inputs using the data in the keyframe table, st-map, render out the st-map for the warp described in the keyframe table. This is useful if you want to bake the results of the node for later. st-map inverse, render out the inverse st-map for the warp in the keyframe table, i.e. the warp from the current frame to the keyframe.

description.text: Select this to render on the Local GPU, if available. You can select this even if no GPU is currently available on your machine. The GPU will then be used whenever the script is opened on a machine which does have a GPU available. You should also select this if you wish to render from the command line with the --gpu option. If this node requires full frames from its inputs, and is therefore unable to reduce its memory overhead, it will fall back to the CPU if an attempt to render a frame on the GPU fails due to lack of memory. When this occurs, a warning message will be printed to the console.
Create, delete or skip to a user keyframe.
This filter is used to create the internal st-map from motion vectors. Some filter types work better for certain types of motion or images, which is why this is a separate filter.

description.plain_text: VectorCornerPin: Uses SmartVectors to warp a cornerpinned image between 'User' keyframes. The user can set keyframes using 'User' and 'From' knobs, similar to the CornerPin node, but between keyframes the Source image will move according to the additional SmartVector input. The 'To' knobs represent where the 'User' knobs have been moved by the SmartVectors between 'User' keyframes.
description.text:
VectorCornerPin: Uses SmartVectors to warp a cornerpinned image between 'User' keyframes.

The user can set keyframes using 'User' and 'From' knobs, similar to the CornerPin node, but between keyframes the Source image will move according to the additional SmartVector input.

The 'To' knobs represent where the 'User' knobs have been moved by the SmartVectors between 'User' keyframes.
